summary: Flat futures on a holiday-thin Monday (bond market closed for Columbus Day), oil back up with Brent near $106, and the week's real tests still ahead (bank earnings Tuesday, CPI Wednesday). Nothing points one way for SPY today, so skip.
reasons: SPY pre-market 778.67 (+0.01% vs 778.57 Friday close, record 781.62); QQQ 750.02 (-0.17%); S&P futures +0.1%, Nasdaq futures -0.1% at 08:00 (ZeroHedge/Reuters). S&P +1.2% last week

Oil: USO +2.4% pre-market; Brent about $106, WTI about $93 (+1%). It first fell on Trump's Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' (not confirmed by Moscow), then rebounded on Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport and more tanker incidents in Hormuz; Iran says Hormuz stays shut until its conditions are met
Rates and dollar: cash Treasuries closed (Columbus Day); 10Y closed 5.24% Friday, Treasury futures a little lower; TLT -0.2% pre-market. UUP +0.3%, DXY near 102.3. Bunds and gilts lower in yield

Calendar: no US data today; Fed's Hammack 12:10 ET; Open Compute Project summit (AMD, NVDA, MRVL in focus). Banks report Tuesday (JPM, WFC, GS, C), CPI Wednesday 10-14 (Reuters: headline +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y; core 0.2% / 2.5%), PPI and retail sales Thursday. FedWatch: about 19% odds of a hike this month

Memory slide: Samsung and SK Hynix fell more than 4% in Seoul (Kospi -3.6%, buyback quotas done, foreign selling); MU -2.2% pre-market (1006.7 vs 1029.0). That is a >= 2% down gap in the rebound_scanner universe on a same-day-expiry Monday, so the champion may fire on MU; the real-option-price retest says this rule is about -39%/trade
Other pre-market: META +1.5% (729.4, no specific news found), MSFT +0.4%, AAPL +0.3%, AMD -0.9%, INTC -1.5%, MRVL -1.4%, AVGO -0.7%, NVDA -0.3%, AMZN/GOOGL -0.2%

AMD dossier: -0.9% gap is under the 2% rebound line; it trades with CPU/semis, and CPU is the weakest theme this week (INTC -12%, ARM -13% 1w). Same-day options Mon/Wed/Fri. META dossier: +1.5% is a small gap with no catalyst found; small gaps mostly fill, so not a sniper pick
VIX level not found in time; Goldman's index-vol desk sees a higher chance of VIX > 25 than of a 2% S&P drop

inputs.overnight: Asia: Kospi -3.6% on memory selling. Europe: yields lower. Oil rebounds as the Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' looks shaky and Gulf shipping attacks continue. US cash bonds closed, so no 2Y/10Y change today; 10Y level is Friday's close

cooling: flash and disk storage (SNDK -8%, STX -8%, WDC -4% 1w; WDC -14% 1m)
rotation.note: Webull daily bars, closes 2026-10-09 vs 10-02 (1w) and 09-10 (1m). Money keeps moving from chips (CPU, memory, storage) into optical, power and the big internet platforms

sniper.catalyst: Bank of America double-upgraded Salesforce to Buy this morning (target $285, about +20% from 238). A two-notch rating change by a major firm is the strongest kind of upgrade; CRM +3.9% pre-market (238.06 vs 229.13), just inside the 4% line, so part of it is already priced. Not a mega cap with same-day options (nearest expiry Friday) and software is not one of the hot themes; on real option prices the strict upgrade rule is only -12%/trade since 2026-01, so this is a catalyst bet, not an evidenced edge. Other upgrades today are small or mid caps (BIIB, FSLR, TYL); META +1.5% has no catalyst found
